Why it matters now

AI is moving fast.Most teams aren't.

The gap between companies that build with AI and those that read about it widens every quarter. The question isn't whether to upskill. It's whether you can afford not to.

Tools exist. Readiness doesn't.

Most enterprises have the AI tools. Very few have teams that can use them on real problems.

Slides don't build capability. Building does.

Generic AI training is forgotten by Monday. Building on actual internal problems sticks.

GCCs are being asked to lead AI experimentation.

Hackathons are the fastest way to surface who can actually lead that shift.

Prototype speed is a competitive advantage.

The fastest teams go from problem statement to working prototype in a weekend.

How It Works

Training that ends in a working prototype.

Not a slide deck. Not a certificate. Something your team actually built on a real problem.

Step 01

Workshop & Demo

Live AI training using tools relevant to your team, with technical and non technical tracks in parallel.

Demos move from screen to desk in days, not weeks.

Step 02

Build on Real Use Cases

Teams solve real problem statements from your business, sourced with stakeholders beforehand.

Ideas move from problem to prototype in hours, not quarters.

Step 03

Mentorship & Support

More than 30 Buildora copilots and domain experts keep teams unblocked through the sprint.

Expert help stays in the sprint, not in status meetings.

Step 04

Evaluation & Report

Structured judging and a post event report with shortlisted solutions and next step recommendations.

Clear reports for leaders, not rough notes that need rewrites.
